steps.stem: Dalia invented a word game: each player says a sentence in which every word meets at least one of two conditions: A. the word contains at least two vowels (a, e, i, o, u); B. the word begins and ends with the same letter. Which of the following sentences does not meet the conditions?
choices: Ronit did enjoy reading novels
Every student likes jazz music
Maria gave twelve roses away
Aviva ate that tomato quietly
explanation: "Jazz" has only one vowel, and its first and last letters differ. In (1) "did" and in (4) "that" have one vowel but begin and end with the same letter, so condition B saves them; in (3) every word has at least two vowels.

steps.stem:
Four candidates applied for a job as a guide at a city museum. These were the results:
- Omer, who speaks English and French, was accepted for the job.
- Yael, who speaks English, was accepted for the job.
- Tamar, who speaks Russian, was not accepted.
- Ido, who speaks Russian and Spanish, was accepted for the job.
Note: none of the four candidates speaks any language other than those listed above. Which of the following could not have been the requirement for being accepted for the job?
choices: Any candidate who speaks two languages is accepted, and any candidate who speaks English is accepted as well
All of the candidates are accepted, except those who speak one language only and that language is not English
A candidate is accepted only if they speak more than one language or do not speak English at all
A candidate who does not speak English is not accepted, unless they speak Spanish
explanation: Under (3) Yael, who speaks English and nothing else, could not be accepted, yet she was. Each of the other requirements fits all four results.

steps.stem: Omri, Talia and Neta live in a three-story building, one on each floor, not necessarily in that order. Each of them keeps one of these pets: a cat, a dog and a rabbit. Given: A. Talia lives on a floor adjacent to the floor of the dog's owner. B. The owner of the rabbit lives on the second floor. Which of the following is necessarily true?
choices: Neta is the owner of the cat
Omri lives on the third floor
Omri is not the owner of the rabbit
Neta is not the owner of the dog
explanation: If Talia lived on the first or third floor, the only floor adjacent to hers would be the second, whose tenant owns the rabbit, not the dog; so Talia lives on the second floor and owns the rabbit. Omri and Neta may be on either of the other floors, with either the cat or the dog.

steps.stem: Two novels and two cookbooks stand on a shelf in places 1 to 4, numbered from left to right. It is known that the two cookbooks do not stand next to each other. Which of the following additional facts would make it possible to determine with certainty the type of every book?
choices: Book 3 is a novel
Book 4 is a cookbook
Book 1 is a novel
No book stands next to a book of its own type
explanation: The cookbooks can stand in places 1 and 3, 1 and 4, or 2 and 4; a novel in place 1 leaves only 2 and 4. (1) and (2) each leave 1 and 4 or 2 and 4, and (4) leaves 1 and 3 or 2 and 4.

steps.stem: The statements made in the following conversation contradict one another. Hadas: "Amit lends his books only to people who are older than he is." Eli: "I am younger than Amit." Rona: "I am older than Eli and younger than Hadas." Amit: "I have lent books to Hadas, to Rona and to Eli." Without which speaker's statement would the conversation still contain a contradiction?
choices: Hadas
Eli
Rona
Amit
explanation: Hadas's and Amit's statements together make Eli older than Amit, while Eli says he is younger; Rona's statement plays no part in this. Removing Hadas, Eli or Amit removes one part of the contradiction.

steps.stem: Maya, Nir and Oren had to choose where their team would spend a day out: at the zoo, at the beach or at the science museum. Each of them expressed a wish. Maya: "I would like us to go to the beach." Nir: "I don't mind where we go, as long as it is not the zoo." Oren: "I will be pleased if we go to the science museum, or if Nir is pleased." The team went to one of the three places, and exactly one of the three did not get their wish. Which of the following is possible?
choices: The team went to the beach
Oren did not get his wish
The team went to the science museum
Nir did not get his wish
explanation: At the museum Maya is disappointed while Nir and Oren are pleased, so exactly one wish fails. At the beach everyone is pleased. Nir's wish fails only at the zoo, and there Maya's and Oren's wishes fail too; Oren's wish fails only when Nir's does, which again happens only at the zoo.

steps.stem: Five contestants take part in a television quiz: Noa, Tal, Yuval, Dana and Ariel. In each round two contestants compete; the loser leaves the quiz, and the winner competes in the next round against a contestant who has not yet competed, until the fourth and last round. The following rule is known: if Noa competes against a contestant who, in the previous round, competed against Tal, Noa loses; in every other case Noa wins. If Noa competed in the first round of the quiz, then -
choices: she lost in the second round
she won the last round
she lost in the first round
she lost in the last round
explanation: Every opponent Noa meets after the first round is a newcomer who did not compete in the previous round, and in the first round there was no previous round; so the rule never makes her lose, and she wins every round including the last.

steps.title: Rules and arrangements — the method
steps.intro: Two question types — rules and arrangements — and combined ones.

tables.title: Rules questions
head: Way
How
rows: Take one answer, test it against every rule
Take one rule, run it through all the answers, cross out

tables.title: Arrangement questions
head: Step
What to do
rows: Circle the items you need to place
Sketch the slots — never solve in your head
Find an anchor: a clue that fixes an exact position
Chain the other clues onto it; loose pairs go at the side
Two items can swap → draw a two-way arc

tips: Each answer adds a new given? Test it alone — start again from the base givens.
Contradiction question: leave one statement out and test whether the rest still clash.
"Exactly N are true": place each answer as the situation and count what holds.

steps.stem: Under the rules of a certain housing cooperative, the board meets once a week, on Tuesday, and any member may ask the board to discuss a particular matter. Such requests must reach the chairperson of the board through the secretary, who is required to pass each request on to the chairperson on the day it is submitted. A matter whose request has reached the chairperson by 5 p.m. on Friday will be placed on the agenda of the following Tuesday; however, if the chairperson determines that the matter needs more preparation than that allows - and only in such a case - she may postpone the discussion to the Tuesday after that, but no later. Four cases of requests to discuss a matter are described below. In which of them were the rules certainly broken?
choices: A member submitted a request to the secretary on a Saturday, and the matter was not discussed on the following Tuesday or on the Tuesday after that, although the secretary passed the request on to the chairperson on the same day

The matter was not discussed on the Tuesday following the request, although the chairperson determined that it needed no extra preparation and although the request was submitted to the secretary on a Friday
The matter was discussed nine days after the request reached the chairperson, although she had not determined that it needed more preparation
A member submitted a request to the secretary on a Wednesday, and the matter was discussed only on the third Tuesday after that, the chairperson having determined that it needed more preparation
explanation: A Wednesday request reaches the chairperson that day, before the Friday deadline, so it must be discussed on the following Tuesday or, if she so determines, on the Tuesday after - never on the third. In (1) the request missed that week's deadline and may have been postponed, in (2) a Friday request may have arrived after 5 p.m., and in (3) a request that reached her on a Sunday is due only nine days later.

steps.stem: Avner, Eitan, Rivka and Tamar are sitting at a square table, one on each side, so that each of them sits opposite one of the others. Given: A. Tamar sits opposite the only man with glasses. B. Avner sits opposite the only woman with a hat. Therefore, it is not possible that -
choices: Tamar does not wear a hat, and Rivka sits beside Eitan
Eitan does not wear glasses, and Avner sits beside Rivka
Avner wears glasses, and Tamar does not wear a hat
Eitan wears glasses, and Avner sits beside Tamar
explanation: If Avner is the man with glasses, Tamar sits opposite him; but the person opposite Avner is the woman with the hat, so Tamar must wear the hat. Each of the other combinations fits some seating.

steps.stem: Lea, Moti, Nili, Oded and Ruth are sitting around a round table (not necessarily in this order). It is known that Nili sits immediately to the left of Oded. Which of the following data would make it possible to determine with certainty how all five are seated?
choices: Lea sits between Oded and Moti, next to both of them
Lea sits between Moti and Ruth, next to both of them
Lea sits next to Nili, and Moti sits next to Ruth
Lea sits next to Ruth, and Moti sits next to Oded
explanation: With Nili and Oded fixed, three seats in a row remain, beginning beside Oded; (1) fills them in the order Lea, Moti, Ruth. Each of the other data leaves two possible seatings.

steps.stem: From the regulations of a certain city: "Every resident of the city must pay an annual waste-removal fee. Notwithstanding the above, a resident is exempt from the fee for 2023 if in that year they were a student - a full-time student under the age of 30 or a part-time student under the age of 25 - and their water consumption that year was below 60 cubic meters. The exemption does not apply, however, if in 2023 the resident ran from their apartment a business that received customers there." For which of the following residents is there not enough information to determine whether they must pay the fee for 2023?
choices: Lior, a full-time student aged 28 in 2023, who ran a hair salon for customers in his apartment and used 45 cubic meters of water
Adi, a full-time student aged 27 in 2023, who ran a design business from her apartment and used 50 cubic meters of water
Guy, a part-time student aged 27 in 2023, who worked as a waiter and used 30 cubic meters of water
Rina, a full-time student aged 22 in 2023, who worked in a bookshop and used 40 cubic meters of water
explanation: Adi meets every condition of the exemption, which is cancelled only if her business received customers at the apartment, and that is not stated. Lior's salon cancels his exemption, Guy is a part-time student over 25 and must pay, and Rina is exempt.

steps.stem: Four cars are parked in a row: two red cars and two white cars. The two white cars are not parked next to each other. Which of the following is necessarily true?
choices: There is a red car at each end of the row
The two red cars are parked next to each other
At least one of the two cars at the ends of the row is white
At least one white car is parked between the two red cars
explanation: The white cars can stand only in places 1 and 3, 1 and 4, or 2 and 4, and in each case one of them is at an end. (1) and (4) fail when the white cars are in places 1 and 4, and (2) fails in the other two cases.

steps.stem: Maya said to Yonatan: "I scored higher than you on the test, but Dror scored higher than I did." Yonatan said to Maya: "Dror scored lower than you, and lower than me too." No two of the three got the same score, and exactly one of the two speakers is lying - that is, stating the opposite of the truth. Which of the following is necessarily true, whether it is Maya or Yonatan who is lying?
choices: The highest score of the three was not Yonatan's
Dror got the highest score of the three
Yonatan's score was lower than Maya's
The lowest score of the three was not Maya's
explanation: If Maya is lying, the truth is Dror below Maya below Yonatan; if Yonatan is lying, it is Yonatan below Maya below Dror. Either way Maya is in the middle. (1), (2) and (3) each hold in only one of the two cases.

steps.stem: Pitzi, Mocha and Lulu are three kittens of different weights. Given: Pitzi is not the heaviest of the three; Lulu is not the lightest. Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
choices: If Mocha is the lightest, then Lulu is the heaviest
If Pitzi is the lightest, then Lulu is the heaviest
Mocha is the heaviest
Pitzi is the lightest
explanation: If Mocha is the lightest, Pitzi and Lulu remain for the top, and Pitzi cannot be the heaviest. (2) fails when Mocha is the heaviest, and (3) and (4) each fail in some order.

steps.stem: Given: A. Gali's salary is not higher than Ofer's salary. B. Gali's salary is not lower than Nurit's salary. Which of the following is not possible?
choices: Gali, Ofer and Nurit all earn the same salary
Ofer's salary is lower than Nurit's salary
Ofer's salary is higher than Nurit's salary
The three salaries are all different
explanation: Nurit earns no more than Gali, and Gali no more than Ofer, so Ofer can never earn less than Nurit. Equal salaries all round and three different salaries are both allowed.

steps.stem: In a certain law office, the files of clients are kept in a single long drawer and arranged from front to back according to three criteria: first by the name of the client's city, then by the client's surname, and then by the year in which the file was opened, as follows. Files of cities whose names begin with A stand in front of files of cities whose names begin with B, and so on; where the first letters are the same, the second letters decide. Within one city, the files are arranged by the client's surname in alphabetical order, and the files of one client by year, the earlier in front. Four files are in the drawer: Mizrahi of Acre, 2016; Barak of Eilat, 2019; Sasson of Eilat, 2012; Barak of Elad, 2014. Which of the four files is at the back of the drawer?
choices: Mizrahi of Acre, 2016
Barak of Eilat, 2019
Sasson of Eilat, 2012
Barak of Elad, 2014
explanation: The city decides first: Acre, then Eilat (E-i), then Elad (E-l). Elad is the last city, and it has only one file. The surname Sasson and the year 2019 matter only within a city.

steps.stem: Noga writes secret messages according to these rules: (a) each word is written backwards; (b) in the result, every A is replaced by I and every I by A; (c) if the original word ended with a vowel, the letter K is added at the beginning of its coded form. Noga wants to send the message NINA LIKES TAPAS. How will she write it?
choices: ANIN SEKIL SAPAT
INAN SEKAL SIPIT
KINAN SEKAL SIPIT
INANK SEKALK SIPITK
explanation: NINA becomes ANIN, then INAN, and since NINA ends with a vowel, KINAN; LIKES becomes SEKIL, then SEKAL; TAPAS becomes SAPAT, then SIPIT. (1) applies only rule (a), (2) forgets rule (c), and (4) puts the K at the end and adds it to every word.

steps.stem: Three friends stand in a row: Yoav at the left end, Keren in the middle and Dvir at the right end. Exactly two of them play the guitar, exactly two play the piano and exactly two play the violin. It is known that: - Yoav plays the violin; - the two guitar players stand next to each other; - the two piano players stand on either side of one of the violin players. Therefore, of the three instruments, Keren plays -
choices: guitar and violin
violin only
guitar only
piano and guitar
explanation: Players on either side of someone can only be the two ends, so Yoav and Dvir play the piano and Keren, in the middle, plays the violin. Two neighbors must include the middle, so Keren also plays the guitar, and she does not play the piano.

steps.stem: A catering company follows these rules when planning a menu: - if a menu includes soup, it must also include bread, and it may not include salad; - if a menu includes fish, it must also include rice, and it may not include soup; - if a menu includes cake, it must also include salad, and it may not include fish. Which of the following menus does not follow the rules?
choices: A menu that includes rice, salad and cake
A menu that includes soup, salad and cake
A menu that includes bread, rice and fish
A menu that includes soup, bread and rice
explanation: A menu that includes soup may not include salad (and needs bread). Each of the other menus meets every rule that applies to it.

steps.stem: Each of the three senior nurses of a hospital ward - Orly, Pnina and Rachel - is either in the ward (at the nurses' station or elsewhere) or out of it (in surgery, escorting a patient to X-ray, or at a meeting). These standing orders are always kept: - when Rachel is in the ward, she stays at the nurses' station only if Orly is in surgery and Pnina is at a meeting; - when Pnina is in the ward, either the other two are in the ward as well, or Rachel is in the ward and Orly is escorting a patient to X-ray. Which of the following situations certainly cannot occur?
choices: Pnina is at a meeting and Orly is escorting a patient to X-ray
Orly is in the ward but not at the nurses' station
Pnina is at the nurses' station and Orly is escorting a patient to X-ray
All three nurses are at the nurses' station
explanation: Rachel may stay at the nurses' station only while Orly is in surgery, so Orly cannot be at the station with her. (3) is allowed by the second part of the second order, and nothing forbids (1) or (2).

steps.stem: Under the rules of a certain college, a student is entitled to a full scholarship if at least one of two conditions holds: - the student's average grade is at least 90 and the student has completed at least two years of studies; - the student's income together with that of the student's parents (the "family income") is lower than an amount defined as the "support threshold." According to the rules, which of the following students is certainly not entitled to a full scholarship?
choices: A student with an average of 95, whose family income is higher than the support threshold
A student with three years of studies, whose family income is higher than the support threshold
A student with an average of 85 and three years of studies, whose parents alone earn more than the support threshold
A student with an average of 92 and four years of studies, whose family income is lower than the support threshold
explanation: An average of 85 rules out the first condition, and if the parents alone earn more than the threshold, the family income does too. (1) may qualify by years of study, which are not stated, (2) may qualify by grades, which are not stated, and (4) qualifies twice over.

steps.stem: Four irrigation channels - Dekel, Oren, Rimon and Shaked, not necessarily in this order - are connected as follows: one of them (channel 1) flows into a second (channel 2); channel 2 and a third channel (channel 3) both flow into the fourth (channel 4), which flows into a reservoir. Three leaves were dropped into the water, not necessarily at the same point, and each drifted downstream until it sank. Two of the leaves drifted along these routes - Leaf A: Oren, then Dekel. Leaf B: Rimon, then Shaked. Which of the following could not have been the route of leaf C?
choices: Shaked, Oren
Dekel, Shaked, the reservoir
Shaked, Dekel
Oren, Dekel, the reservoir
explanation: The only two flows that share no channel are 1 into 2 and 3 into 4, so leaves A and B took these two, in one order or the other. Either Oren and Dekel are 1 and 2 and Rimon and Shaked are 3 and 4, or the reverse; in neither case does Shaked flow into Oren. Each of the other routes fits one of the two cases.

steps.stem: On every day on which Itai does not work a night shift at the factory where he is employed - and only on such days - he picks up his daughter from kindergarten in the afternoon. On those days he always walks to the kindergarten at four o'clock, unless the temperature at that hour is above 35 degrees, in which case he does not walk there but drives there instead. Which of the following could happen?
choices: On Sunday the temperature at four o'clock was 30 degrees, and Itai drove to the kindergarten
On Wednesday the temperature at four o'clock was 38 degrees, and Itai did not drive to the kindergarten
On Monday Itai worked a night shift, and at four o'clock he drove to the kindergarten to pick up his daughter
On Tuesday Itai did not work a night shift, the temperature at four o'clock was 28 degrees, and Itai did not walk to the kindergarten
explanation: If Itai worked a night shift that day, he did not go to the kindergarten at all, so on a hot day he may well not have driven there. In (1) it was not hot enough to drive, in (3) the night shift rules out the pickup, and in (4) nothing excuses him from walking.

steps.stem: At a certain research institute the following rule applies: the last person to leave any laboratory must turn off its air conditioner, and whoever is the last to leave the building must turn off every air conditioner left on anywhere in the building. One evening Yaron was the last to leave the building. He noticed that the air conditioner was on in one of the laboratories - a laboratory in which only Michal had worked that day - and he left without turning it off. Which of the following claims is correct?
choices: Neither Yaron nor Michal broke the rule
Yaron broke the rule, but Michal did not
Both Yaron and Michal broke the rule
Yaron did not break the rule, but Michal did
explanation: Michal was the last to leave her laboratory and left its air conditioner on; Yaron was the last to leave the building and left it on as well.

steps.stem: The city's regulations contain three clauses on shop signs. Clause 1: "A neon sign may be hung only on a shop front up to 8 meters wide." Clause 2: "A large sign may be hung only on a shop front up to 12 meters wide." Clause 3: "Only a shop front up to 4 meters wide may display a small wooden sign." A shop owner argued that the answer to a question that interested her could not be known with certainty from any one clause on its own. Which of the following could be that question?
choices: May a shop front 3 meters wide carry a large neon sign?
May a shop front 8 meters wide carry a small neon sign?
May a shop front 12 meters wide carry a large neon sign?
May a shop front 4 meters wide carry a small wooden sign?
explanation: "Large" and "neon" fall under different clauses, and only the two together settle the question. (2) and (3) are settled by clause 1 alone, and (4) by clause 3 alone.

steps.stem: A cake is made of three layers - chocolate, vanilla and strawberry - of different thicknesses, placed one on top of another. It is known that: - the thickest layer is next to the vanilla layer; - the chocolate layer is neither the thickest nor the thinnest. From this it necessarily follows that -
choices: the top layer is strawberry
the thinnest layer is not vanilla
the middle layer is not chocolate
the chocolate layer and the strawberry layer are not next to each other
explanation: Chocolate is of middle thickness, so the thickest layer is strawberry or vanilla; it is next to vanilla, so it is strawberry, and vanilla is the thinnest. Strawberry and vanilla are next to each other, so chocolate cannot be between them and must be at the top or the bottom. (1) and (4) are possible but not necessary, and (2) is false.

steps.stem: The computer system that controls the watering, spraying and ventilation of a large greenhouse operates according to three rules, which were written by its designers: A. The system may not harm a plant, and must do all it can to prevent harm to a plant. B. The system must carry out the grower's instructions, unless they conflict with rule A. C. The system must save water, unless this conflicts with rule A or rule B. There are cases, however, in which the rules make conflicting demands on the system, and it cannot decide how it should act. Which of the following situations is an example of such a case?
choices: Two growers who share the greenhouse each instruct the system to uproot the other's plants
Pests are attacking a plant, and the only way the system can stop them is to spray a substance that will harm the plant next to it
A grower instructs the system to water all the plants twice a day, although once a day is enough
A plant is wilting and the system could water it, but a grower instructs it not to
explanation: Rule A both forbids harming a plant and demands preventing harm, and here the two halves collide. In (1) and (4) rule A overrides the instructions, and in (3) rule B overrides rule C.

steps.stem: In a certain region there are two ferry lines (ferry X and ferry Y) and two train lines (the green line and the orange line). It is known that: - no station is shared by the two ferry lines, and no station is shared by the two train lines; - ferry Y and the orange line have no station in common; - ferry X and the green line have only one station in common, and at that station the ferry only lets passengers off and does not take any on. A tourist traveled on all four lines, once on each, changing lines only at shared stations and using no other means of transport. Which line did the tourist travel on first?
choices: Ferry X
Ferry Y
The orange line
The green line
explanation: The only possible changes are between the orange line and ferry X, from ferry X to the green line (one way only), and between the green line and ferry Y. A route through all four lines must therefore run orange line, ferry X, green line, ferry Y.

steps.stem: At a certain university, two bodies are authorized to decide on students' requests: the faculty committee and the university committee. Different arrangements apply to different kinds of request, and they determine which body is authorized to decide: A. Exclusive authority - only one of the two bodies is authorized to decide on the request. B. Parallel authority - both bodies are authorized, but once one of them has begun to deal with the request, the other may not deal with it. C. Authority by consent - only the faculty committee is authorized, unless the student and the lecturer have both agreed to bring the request before the university committee. A request to change an exam grade is under the exclusive authority of the faculty committee; a request for an extension on a paper is under parallel authority; a request for exemption from a course is under authority by consent. Which of the following situations is possible?
choices: The student and the lecturer agreed that the university committee would decide on a request to change an exam grade, and it does so
The student and the lecturer disagree about which body should decide on a request for exemption from a course, and the university committee decides it
The faculty committee began to deal with a request for an extension on a paper, and at the student's request the university committee began to deal with it too
The student and the lecturer agreed that the university committee would decide on a request for exemption from a course, and it does so
explanation: Consent of both sides opens the university committee to a request for exemption. (1) breaks the faculty committee's exclusive authority, (2) lacks the required consent, and (3) breaks the bar that parallel authority sets.

steps.stem: Noga, Hadas and Efrat, three sisters of different ages, are sitting on a bench (not necessarily in this order). It is known that: - Noga is older than the sister sitting at the left end; - Hadas is older than the sister sitting in the middle. Therefore, necessarily -
choices: Hadas is sitting at the right end
Efrat is not sitting at the right end
Hadas is older than Noga
Efrat is older than Noga
explanation: Noga is not at the left end and Hadas is not in the middle, which leaves two seatings: Efrat, Noga, Hadas (Hadas older than Noga, Noga older than Efrat) and Hadas, Efrat, Noga (Noga older than Hadas, Hadas older than Efrat). In both, Efrat is the youngest and not at the right end; (1) and (3) hold in only one seating, and (4) in neither.

steps.stem: A company makes plant-food mixtures for houseplant problems. Each mixture contains two of the four salts the company uses - P, Q, R and S - and its label names the problems it is suited to. The company considers a mixture suited to a problem if at least one of its two salts relieves the problem and neither of them is liable to worsen it. It is known that: - only P relieves yellowing, and only S is liable to worsen it; - only Q relieves drooping, and only P is liable to worsen it; - only R relieves brown tips, and only Q is liable to worsen them; - only S relieves root rot, and only R is liable to worsen it. The label of a certain mixture says that it is suited to two different problems. Which two could they be?
choices: Drooping and yellowing
Brown tips and root rot
Root rot and yellowing
Yellowing and brown tips
explanation: A mixture of P and R relieves yellowing and brown tips, and neither salt worsens either problem. Every other pair of problems calls for two salts one of which worsens the other's problem.

steps.stem: When Hila orders dessert at her favorite café, the waiter offers her two desserts she has not yet tasted, and she chooses one of them. It is known that: A. Hila prefers cakes to ice creams, and ice creams to fruit salads. B. When she is offered two desserts of the same kind, she prefers the cheaper one. C. If one of the desserts contains pistachio, Hila chooses it regardless of its kind or its price. Yesterday Hila chose a vanilla ice cream that cost 28 shekels. Which of the following could have been the dessert offered to her together with it?
choices: A strawberry ice cream with chocolate sauce that cost 32 shekels
A lemon cake with whipped cream that cost 34 shekels
A chocolate ice cream with whipped cream that cost 22 shekels
A fruit salad topped with chopped pistachios that cost 30 shekels
explanation: Of two ice creams Hila takes the cheaper, so a 32-shekel one loses to the vanilla. (2) would have won by kind, (3) by price and (4) by its pistachios.

steps.stem: Ilan has three marbles: two blue and one green. Maya also has three marbles: one blue, one red and one green. Ilan gave Maya one of his marbles in exchange for one of hers. After the exchange, each of them had two marbles of one color and a third marble of another color. Which of the following could not have happened?
choices: Ilan received Maya's blue marble
Maya received one of Ilan's blue marbles
Maya received Ilan's green marble
Ilan received Maya's green marble
explanation: If Ilan received a blue marble, either he gave his green one and was left with three blue marbles, or he gave a blue one and nothing changed, leaving Maya with three colors. Each of the other exchanges has a version that meets the condition.

steps.stem: Three kinds of caterpillar - A, B and C - feed on the leaves of three kinds of tree: mulberry, fig and grape. Kind A feeds only on fig and grape leaves; kind B feeds only on mulberry and fig leaves; kind C feeds only on mulberry and grape leaves. In a biology lesson, the teacher put one caterpillar of each kind in a separate box with leaves of all three trees, and at the end of the lesson checked which leaves each caterpillar had eaten. Which of the following cannot be?
choices: None of the caterpillars ate mulberry leaves
All three caterpillars ate the same kind of leaf
Two of the caterpillars ate a kind of leaf that the third did not eat
Each caterpillar ate two kinds of leaf
explanation: No kind of leaf is eaten by all three kinds of caterpillar: each leaf is refused by exactly one of them. Each of the other outcomes is possible.
